name: Kasa Smart Plug Slim with Energy Monitoring KP125M

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). The datasheet lists Bluetooth for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link calls it Kasa's first Matter-certified plug. We did not find a CSA listing that names the KP125M model number.

apple_home.note: Set up in Apple Home by scanning the Matter code. We found no separate HomeKit (HAP) support for this model.

google_home.note: Set up in the Google Home app through Matter; needs a Google Matter controller.

alexa.note: TP-Link says Matter Kasa devices connect to Alexa directly and don't need the Kasa skill. Needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings; setup is through Matter.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the KP125M (with a footnote). It can also be added through the Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: Likely works with the Kasa app alone, but we found no official page that says so outright. The datasheet says Matter use needs a Matter controller.

localControl.note: TP-Link says it keeps LAN control between devices even if the home internet goes offline.

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical use in the Kasa (or Tapo) app. Users report that Matter exposes only on/off, not power readings; we found no official statement on Matter energy data.

maxLoadWatts.note: 15 A / 1800 W for general use and resistive loads at 100–120 V; 1/6 HP motor.

summary: The Kasa KP125M is a slim US Wi-Fi plug with energy monitoring that reaches Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings through Matter. TP-Link says Matter Kasa devices join Alexa directly rather than through the Kasa skill. Home Assistant can use its TP-Link integration or Matter. It runs on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, is rated 15 A / 1800 W, and keeps LAN control if the internet drops.
caveats: Energy readings show in the Kasa or Tapo app; users report Matter platforms only get on/off.
Matter pairing is only open for 15 minutes after power-up; power-cycle the plug if setup times out.
Alexa needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller; the Kasa skill doesn't cover Matter Kasa devices.
